changes: Added daily automatic admin password reset (daily-password.sh): calls the local reset API in auto mode every day at 3:30 AM via cron and sends the new password to Telegram

The daily Telegram notification edits a single stored message instead of sending a new one each day - the message ID is kept in tg_password_message_id; if the message is deleted, a new one is sent and its ID saved again
Added TG_DAILY_PASSWORD toggle to .env/.env.example to enable or disable the daily password reset
install.sh now downloads daily-password.sh and schedules its cron job alongside the update check; uninstall.sh removes both cron jobs
Removed the stale PUBLIC_BIND variable from .env.example (the toggle was removed in 1.2.1 and the server never reads it)
Removed the PUBLIC_BIND toggle - the API now always listens on 0.0.0.0; install.sh unconditionally opens the API port in ufw/firewalld
Fixed the version banner in install.sh showing a stale version from a previously cached config.sh (banner now prints after config.sh is downloaded)
Made install.sh's port-listening check reliable: retry loop over ss/netstat with an HTTP probe fallback instead of a single netstat/ss grep that could report false negatives

uninstall.sh now performs a full removal: systemd service, daily update cron job, firewall rule for the API port, and optionally (confirmed interactively or via --yes) the entire deploy directory including .env

install.sh now detects CDN/proxy redirect pages (e.g. a Cloudflare rule rickrolling raw file downloads) saved as downloaded files: HTML content is rejected, and .env.example is validated to contain API_KEY/API_PORT before use - otherwise it falls back to generating a local template instead of copying a garbage page into .env
Fixed inconsistent version numbers across install.sh, config.sh, version.json and api_server.py that caused the update checker to compare against the wrong current version
Fixed install.sh's fallback SERVICE_NAME being self-referential (resolved to an empty string) when config.sh was unavailable, which broke systemctl calls during install
Fixed update.sh using 'local' outside of a function during the clean-install hash re-check step, which raised a bash error and skipped SHA256 verification
Hardened API key comparison in api_server.py to use a constant-time check (hmac.compare_digest) instead of '==', preventing timing-based key guessing

Fixed install.sh making the deployment directory world-writable (chmod 777); it is now owner-only (700), and .env is locked to 600 - closes a local privilege-escalation path since the API server and update scripts in that directory run as root via systemd and cron
Removed logging of partial API key values on authentication failures to stop secret material from leaking into logs
API_KEY is now required: the server fails closed and refuses every request when unset, instead of running unauthenticated
Removed flask-cors and the wildcard CORS policy - this API has no legitimate browser caller
Added per-IP rate limiting (10 requests / 5 minutes) on the reset endpoint, keyed on the raw connection IP so it can't be bypassed via X-Forwarded-For
Replaced the Flask development server with waitress; added PUBLIC_BIND (default false = 127.0.0.1-only) so the API is no longer bound to 0.0.0.0 and firewall-opened by default

Added strict container_id validation (Docker's own naming syntax) before it ever reaches docker exec, plus a `--` argument separator in reset-password-helper.sh, closing a docker-exec argument-injection precondition
Tightened auto-mode container discovery to an exact image match instead of a substring match
Replaced predictable /tmp file and directory names in update.sh/install.sh with mktemp, removing a local symlink-race precondition; .env backups now inherit mktemp's owner-only permissions
Pinned dependencies to floor/ceiling version ranges (Flask, python-dotenv, waitress) and raised the minimum Python requirement to 3.9+ to match them; install.sh now checks this before proceeding
Removed the webbrowser-open easter egg on unauthorized requests and trimmed generic exception text returned to callers
Fixed an unbound-variable crash in install.sh (API_KEY was never assigned before the set -u check that decides whether to generate one)
Added GET /api/v1/panel-status, proxying Dokploy's own settings.health endpoint so callers can check the panel is actually up before requesting a reset; added DOKPLOY_URL to .env
Added centralized configuration file (config.sh) for common settings
Improved configuration management across all scripts
Centralized version management in config.sh
Test version for update system verification
Added automatic update system with version checking
Added update.sh script for checking and installing new versions
Added support for AUTOMATICALLY_CHECK_FOR_NEW_UPDATES in .env file
Added Telegram notifications for new version availability
Added daily update check via cron job (runs at 2:00 AM)
Added clean installation process during updates (removes old files)
Added changelog display in logs and Telegram notifications
Improved version comparison and update logic
Added .env file backup and restore during updates
Fixed API_PORT configuration to always use 11292
Added backup of previous version before update (saved to /tmp/reset-password-backup-*)
Added aggressive file cleanup during updates (removes all old files and directories)
Added download verification (checks file size and validates install script)
Added detailed logging with timestamps for update process
Improved error handling and recovery during updates
Added SHA256 hash verification for install.sh file integrity check
Added retry mechanism for downloads (3 attempts with exponential backoff)
Added installation verification (checks service status and port availability)
Added automatic hash comparison against server-provided SHA256 hash
Enhanced security with file integrity verification before installation
